content.text:
## Plan: AI gradient global helper plugin

TL;DR — add an opt-in global helper utility that emits the same AI gradient treatment as the custom agent-shell border/background without requiring a wrapper component. The implementation should follow the repo’s `defineUtility` + `globalModifierSelector` pattern and preserve composition with existing border-width, radius, and background utilities.

### Steps
1. Confirm the public surface and package placement
   - Recommended: a dedicated helper plugin or an extension of the existing custom-components package, depending on whether you want a narrower API surface or a single “extras” bundle.
   - Because these are global classes, not component-specific rules, they should remain opt-in and not alter any existing component defaults.

2. Reuse the agent-shell gradient contract
   - Mirror the styling pattern in [plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/components/agent-shell/agent-shell.css](plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/components/agent-shell/agent-shell.css):
     - use a base fill plus a layered AI gradient
     - keep the border transparent with `border: <width> solid transparent`
     - set `background-origin: border-box`
     - set `background-clip: padding-box, border-box`
   - This ensures `--border-width-*`, `border-radius`, and background modifiers still behave as expected.

3. Implement the global helper classes
   - Pattern after [formats/components/src/utilities/layout/index.ts](formats/components/src/utilities/layout/index.ts) and [formats/components/src/utilities/mask/index.ts](formats/components/src/utilities/mask/index.ts).
   - Emit selectors equivalent to:
     - `.--border-color-ai`
     - `.--border-color-ai-horizontal`
     - `.--background-ai`
     - `.--background-ai-horizontal`
   - The border variant should layer the gradient as a border effect; the background variant should apply it to the element’s background instead.

4. Add directional behavior
   - Default vertical direction remains top-to-bottom to match the custom AI shell treatment.
   - Horizontal variant flips direction by language:
     - LTR: `linear-gradient(to left, ...)`
     - RTL: `linear-gradient(to right, ...)`
   - This should be done with logical direction handling, not hard-coded `left`/`right` values in the default rule.

5. Expose the helpers through the plugin
   - Create a helper export function, following the existing plugin export pattern in [plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/index.ts).
   - Keep the API small and declarative, with the CSS generation isolated to the helper rule set.

6. Verify with focused checks
   - Add CSS assertions or a targeted test that confirms:
     - each selector is emitted
     - the directional rule changes with `dir="rtl"`
     - border width + radius composition still works
     - no default component styling is mutated

### Relevant files
- [plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/components/agent-shell/agent-shell.css](plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/components/agent-shell/agent-shell.css) — source of the border/background gradient pattern
- [formats/components/src/utilities/layout/index.ts](formats/components/src/utilities/layout/index.ts) — prior art for global utility generation
- [formats/components/src/utilities/mask/index.ts](formats/components/src/utilities/mask/index.ts) — prior art for global class utility exports
- [plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/index.ts) — plugin export style
- [formats/components/src/index.ts](formats/components/src/index.ts) — public API shape and registration pattern

### Verification
1. Run the relevant generated CSS tests after implementing the helper selectors.
2. Do a quick local preview check to confirm the gradient border and background render correctly with `--border-width-*`, `border-radius`, and RTL/LTR flips.

### Decisions
- Keep the helper opt-in and global-only, because this is a reusable surface treatment, not a component default.
- Reuse the existing agent-shell gradient recipe for consistency with the current custom component.
- Avoid coupling the helper to a specific component class so it can be layered onto any container.

### Further considerations
1. Decide whether this should ship as a dedicated helper package or be folded into the custom-components bundle.
2. Confirm the final naming convention matches the established global utility forms (`.--...`), especially because this repo already combines bare and chained global modifiers via `globalModifierSelector`.

## ✅ Fix for the AI-secondary button glyph and border override

I fixed both issues in the shared button rules:

- The explicit icon glyph for `.-color-ai-secondary.-icon-*` now keeps the AI gradient instead of falling back to white/transparent.
- `.-color-ai-secondary.-without-border` now hides the gradient ring via `::after`, so the border no longer remains visible.

Updated areas:
- [formats/components/src/components/button/button.css](formats/components/src/components/button/button.css)
- [formats/components/tests/components/button.test.ts](formats/components/tests/components/button.test.ts)

### Root cause
The AI-secondary icon rule was overriding the background with `currentColor`, which resolves to the inherited transparent text color on the button. I changed it to use the same AI gradient as the base secondary glyph.

The border issue came from the `::after` ring still being painted even when `-without-border` removed the button border; the ring was never explicitly suppressed.
